outcome: Mark a milestone complete, recorded only after a re-read
acceptance_criteria: The control follows the server only: with the options body `can_complete: true`, "Mark complete" is present; with `can_complete: false` it is absent, whatever the user's role label says — verify: `tests/milestone-complete.test.tsx` renders both bodies for the same persona and asserts the button; `grep -rniE "pmo lead|isPmo|role" frontend/src/features/projects/MilestoneComplete.tsx frontend/src/features/projects/useMilestoneComplete.ts` finds no role check.

Each hold shows its plain-word text and no control: `baseline_required`, `proof_required`, `name_in_use`, and `can_complete:false` with `hold:null` — verify: test asserts text and `queryByRole('button', {name: 'Mark complete'})` is null for each; the raw hold codes never appear in the DOM.
With `can_complete: true` and no evidence chosen, or the confirmation unticked, the button is disabled — verify: test asserts `disabled` for each missing piece and enabled when all are present.

Choosing an existing proof and pressing sends exactly one `POST …/milestones/completions` with body `{revision, name, evidence_id}` and header `X-CSRFToken`, and no `upload_id` or `checked` — verify: test spies on `fetch` and asserts the count and exact JSON.

Choosing a PDF first sends `POST /api/v1/cases/<id>/files` as multipart with `file`, then (after both checkboxes) `POST …/completions` with `{revision, name, upload_id, checked: true}`; `checked` is never sent without the second checkbox — verify: test asserts request bodies and order; asserts the PDF zone is absent when `can_attach_pdf` is false.
Double activation (click twice, Enter then click) sends one POST — verify: test fires two clicks before the mock resolves and asserts one completions POST.

"Recorded" appears only after the re-read: after a 201, before the `GET …/milestones/<id>` resolves the page shows "Checking the record…" and not "Milestone recorded"; when the re-read fails (`reread-fail`) the page shows "couldn't confirm it yet" with "Check again", never "recorded", and "Check again" issues only a GET — verify: test with a deferred re-read, then the `reread-fail` mock case; asserts no second POST.

The Recorded view's name, date and "Proof version" come from the re-read body, not the 201 — verify: test serves different `name` casing/`proof_version` in the re-read and asserts the re-read values are shown; a re-read whose `name` differs from the written name does not show "recorded".

A 409 keeps the person's input and reloads: after `conflict` the options are re-read once with `?name=`, the new `revision` is used on the next press, the chosen proof, uploaded PDF and ticked boxes remain, the 409 message shows, and no POST is made until the person presses again — verify: test counts requests (one POST, one options GET) and asserts the form state; then press and assert the second POST carries the new revision.

An uncertain failure (network error or 503) shows "We couldn't tell whether this was recorded" and sends no second POST on its own (wait past a fake-timer advance of 60 s) — verify: test with `uncertain` and fake timers asserts one POST total. "Check again" issues a GET options only; for `uncertain-saved` it says a completion with this name is now recorded and does not show "Milestone recorded" for this press; for `uncertain` it says it wasn't recorded and returns the form with input kept.

403 on the write shows "You can't mark this milestone complete." and keeps input; 404, 401, 400/422, 413, 415 and 429 show their wording above; 401 shows `SignedOutState` — verify: one test per status using a `fetch` stub.

Options read 403/404/5xx/guard failure on the page shows the no-access card or `WorkErrorCard` with Try again, and no control; no partial data is drawn — verify: tests with the `forbidden`, `notfound` cases and an invalid body (missing `can_attach_pdf`).

Completion never starts an invoice: no "Start the invoice", "Chidi drafts", "invoice started" or invoice number appears on the page in any state, and the page issues no request to any `billing-invoices` or work-start route — verify: `grep -rniE "start the invoice|chidi" frontend/src/features/projects/MilestoneComplete.tsx` has no match; test asserts the Recorded text equals the "What happens next" wording and the fetch log has only the files POST, completions GET/POST and milestone GET.

The Milestones tab shows "Mark complete" only on rows with `completed_at: null` and only when the tab's unnamed options read gives `can_complete: true`; the link goes to `…/milestones/complete?name=<encoded label>`; a hold shows its reason once above the table; an options-read failure leaves F-71's table and completions unchanged — verify: extend `tests/milestones.test.tsx` (F-71's file) with these cases; a completed row never has the link.
No name in the URL shows "Choose a milestone from the Milestones tab." and makes no request — verify: test with an empty `name` and an over-200-character `name`; assert `fetch` call count 0.
A "Show more" on proofs requests `?name=<name>&page=2` and appends without duplicating ids — verify: test with `paged`.
Every mock body served for the new routes validates against `contracts/psl-factory.openapi.json` 1.24.0 — verify: new Ajv test, as in `tests/mock-live-projects.test.ts`, covers each case above.

Phone (390 px): one column, "Mark complete" at the foot, 44 px tap targets, no horizontal scroll — verify: browser check of `/projects/<id>/milestones/complete?name=…` at 1440 and 390 against `SCR-19-desktop` and `SCR-19-mobile`.

Live smoke (integration owner), Django 8010: with an account whose options read gives `can_complete: true`, one real completion records, the re-read returns the same `id`, and a second visit shows `name_in_use`; with an account that gets `can_complete: false` there is no control — verify: recorded in build.md with the account names and responses.

LB-2 is named in the PR description as flagged: "PMO Lead enforcement on POST milestones/completions is unconfirmed server-side; the screen follows `can_complete` and invents no role rule" — verify: the PR body contains the text, and `delivery/connect/backend-questions.md` "New from lanes" has an LB-2 line (the coordinator adds it if missing).

risk.rationale: High. A completion is an irreversible, billing-adjacent write that queues a Finance handoff (contract 1.24.0, backend-answers B-28 to B-31). Surfaces: ui and api for the screen and write. auth because authority rests on the server's `can_complete` and LB-2 is unconfirmed. contract-change for the 1.24.0 options and write. product-decision for D-187 and the PSL PMO Lead rule. The UI adds no authority, so the residual risk is the backend gap, which is flagged and not hidden.

findings.summary: The PDF zone is not PDF-only. Spec "Control": "a `FileUpload` ("Or upload a private PDF", `.pdf` only, `PROOF_MAX_BYTES`)", with 413 "That file is too large to upload." and 415 "Only a PDF can be attached as proof." Actual: `EvidencePicker` (src/features/workspace/EvidencePicker.tsx:38) passes no `accept`, so `FileUpload` falls back to `PROOF_TYPES` = `.pdf,.png,.jpg,.jpeg,.eml` (src/components/FileUpload.tsx:18,89). `uploadCaseFile`'s `refuseFile` allows the same list (src/features/workspace/evidence.ts:16-21). A PNG can be uploaded and sent as the `upload_id` proof of a completion that queues the Finance handoff. The upload errors also use the picker's wording ("That file is too large.", "That file type isn’t accepted.") instead of the spec's. The input's accessible name is "Evidence file", not "Or upload a private PDF", because the visible span is not tied to the input. Path: src/features/projects/MilestoneComplete.tsx:213-226. Expected: use `FileUpload` with `accept={['.pdf']}` together with `uploadCaseFile`, plus the spec's 413/415/429 wording and label. Or ask lane C for an `accept`/label prop on `EvidencePicker`. Add a test that a `.png` is refused before any request.

findings.summary: The second confirmation is not bound to the file it confirms. Steps: upload file A, tick "I have checked this file is the proof for this milestone.", press Remove, upload file B. Spec: "Ticking it is what sets `checked: true` in the body"; AC 5 says "`checked` is never sent without the second checkbox". Expected: clear `fileChecked` whenever `upload` changes (a new file or a removal); a 409 reload keeps the same file and keeps the tick. Add a test for remove, re-upload and the box unticked.

Problem: the page takes `name` from the URL query (`MilestoneCompleteRoute.tsx:11`), and the server accepts any non-empty, unique name. `guard_complete` (`apps/pmo/services.py:137`) does not bind the name to a configured SOW milestone; `tests/test_factory_api.py:139` records "Synthetic completion". The client checks the trimmed length but sends the raw string (`milestonesModel.ts:107`), and the server compares raw names. So a crafted link like `?name=UAT%20sign-off%20`, or a case variant, could record a second completion of the same stage. That gets past the `name_in_use` duplicate guard and queues a second Finance handoff (`Outbox`). An authorised person still has to choose a proof, tick the box and press, with the name shown. Expected: the server accepts only the exact configured milestone identity, as B-28 implies. Optionally the UI could offer only names that equal an uncompleted `/money` label. Actual: any 1 to 200 character string is recorded.

findings.summary: A 429 on the PDF upload shows lane C's "Try again shortly." instead of the standard `rate_limited` wording the spec asks for. The spec ("Control": "429 the standard `rate_limited` wording") means "Too many requests. Try again shortly." (src/api/errors.ts:38). `pdfUploadMessage` maps only `too_large` and `unsupported`, and everything else falls through to `uploadErrorMessage` (src/features/projects/MilestoneComplete.tsx:47-51; src/features/workspace/evidence.ts `uploadErrorMessage`). Expected: map `rate_limited` to the standard message in `pdfUploadMessage`, and add a third row to the 413/415 `it.each`.

The read-only Project and Milestone values are plain `<div aria-labelledby=…>` elements (MilestoneComplete.tsx:171,177). ARIA 1.2 does not allow `aria-labelledby` on an element with no role, so assistive technology ignores it and axe reports `aria-prohibited-attr`. The visible text still reads correctly. Expected: use a `<dl>`/`<dt>`/`<dd>` pair, or drop the attribute. This is UI-1-2's markup; the UI reviewer may prefer to own it.

The test "TECH-1-4: … the form stays busy until the reload settles" (tests/milestone-complete.test.tsx:426) only checks the "couldn't reload" message. It never holds the reload open to check that the button is busy, or that a second press during the reload sends nothing. The code is correct: useMilestoneComplete.ts:183-189 awaits `reload(true)` before it clears `inFlight` and goes back to idle. Expected: put the options read behind a gate, press again during the reload, and assert one POST and `aria-busy`.
